newsitem.title: USA: Anaheim, Calif., says downgrade will not cost city.
newsitem.headline: Anaheim, Calif., says downgrade will not cost city.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Inc's decision to downgrade Anaheim, Calif., debt should not increase the southern California city's borrowing costs, a city spokesman said on Thursday.
"Of course we're disappointed," Anaheim spokesman Bret Colson said. "But it has no immediate impact on us because we have no plans to issue any general obligation bonds."

Earlier on Thursday, Moody's said it downgraded the rating on the city of Anaheim's general obligation bonds from Aa1 to Aa2 to reflect the implications of Proposition 218, approved by state voters in November.

"The city previously had significant discretionary capacity under its charter powers to levy taxes against additional sectors of the local economy," Moody's said. "This considerable revenue flexibility has been significantly limited by Proposition 218, which amended the state Constitution to require voter approval of any tax increase."
Anaheim said the downgrade would have no impact on its issuance plans.
Several other California cities have been downgraded by the major rating agencies following Proposition 218's passage.
